record.paper_title: (E,E′N) and (E,E′NN) Experiments at NIKHEF, Mainz and JLab and Open Problems in One- and Two-Nucleon Emissions
record.original_question: What reaction mechanisms generate the enhanced transverse strength and nearly momentum-independent high-missing-momentum cross section seen in exclusive 16O(e,e′p) measurements at high missing energy, where distorted-wave one-nucleon knockout underpredicts the data and two-nucleon emission channels contribute substantially? More broadly, where exactly does the single-particle picture of one-nucleon knockout break down as missing momentum and missing energy increase?

evidence.quote: There is accumulating evidence for enhanced (e,e′p) transverse strength of non-single particle origin at high missing energies.

For pm > 200 MeV the cross section is almost constant, (e,e′pp) and (e,e′pn) contributing by about one half of the measured cross section. Besides testing the limits of the single-particle model in one-nucleon knockout, experiments are also proposed to directly observe two nucleons ejected in coincidence with the scattered electron.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the exclusive electron-induced proton knockout reaction on an oxygen-16 target, $^{16}\mathrm{O}(e,e'p)$, in which an incident electron scatters and is detected in coincidence with an ejected proton, leaving a residual nucleus. Denote by $p_m$ the missing momentum and by $E_m$ the missing energy reconstructed from the kinematics of the detected electron and proton. In the standard distorted-wave impulse approximation (DWIA) "single-particle" picture, the cross section factorizes into a kinematic factor, the off-shell electron-proton cross section, and a distorted single-particle spectral function describing the removed proton.

Experimental observations in the regime of high missing energy include: (i) the longitudinal/transverse-separated cross section exhibits an enhanced transverse component that cannot be reproduced by DWIA one-nucleon knockout from bound shell-model orbitals; (ii) for missing momenta $p_m \gtrsim 200\ \mathrm{MeV}/c$ the differential cross section becomes nearly independent of $p_m$; and (iii) coincidence measurements of two outgoing nucleons, $^{16}\mathrm{O}(e,e'pp)$ and $^{16}\mathrm{O}(e,e'pn)$, account for roughly half of the inclusive-in-final-state $(e,e'p)$ strength in this region.

Problem. Identify and quantitatively characterize the reaction mechanisms responsible for the enhanced transverse strength and the flat, nearly momentum-independent high-$p_m$ cross section observed in $^{16}\mathrm{O}(e,e'p)$ at high $E_m$. In particular, determine the relative contributions of:
(a) short-range central and tensor nucleon–nucleon correlations in the initial-state wave function,
(b) meson-exchange currents (two-body electromagnetic currents),
(c) intermediate $\Delta$-isobar and other resonance currents,
(d) final-state interactions and rescattering of the knocked-out nucleon,
and establish, as functions of $p_m$ and $E_m$, the kinematic boundary beyond which the single-particle DWIA description of one-nucleon knockout ceases to be valid.
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent theoretical work (e.g., the Pavia and Ghent groups) has identified tensor correlations as the dominant source of pn knockout strength and meson-exchange/isobar currents as the principal source of transverse strength at deep missing energies, with refined two-nucleon knockout calculations reproducing much of the (e,e'pn) data. However, a complete, quantitative decomposition of the high-$E_m$, high-$p_m$ cross section into correlation, MEC, $\Delta$, and FSI contributions across the full kinematic domain — and a precise demarcation of where the single-particle picture fails — remains incomplete.

status_evidence.title: Spin-dependent correlations and the semi-exclusive 16O(e,e'p) reaction
status_evidence.snippet: Tensor correlations produce substantially more semi-exclusive (e,e'p) strength than central correlations and are predominantly manifest in the proton–neutron knockout channel.
status_evidence.claim: Tensor correlations dominate the high-Em (e,e'p) strength via the pn channel.

status_evidence.title: Knockout of proton-neutron pairs from 16O with electromagnetic probes
status_evidence.snippet: Improvements to the Pavia model of two-nucleon knockout from 16O give calculated cross sections in much better agreement with (e,e'pn) data.
status_evidence.claim: Two-nucleon knockout models now reproduce a substantial portion of the (e,e'pn) data, partially accounting for the strength missing from DWIA one-nucleon knockout.
